title: Hosea Bible Quiz - Chapter 8
description: Ten questions on Hosea 8: the trumpet and the eagle, the calf of Samaria, and sowing the wind to reap the whirlwind.

questions.text: What is said to be over Yahweh's house in the opening verse?
questions.explanation: The verse says to put the trumpet to your lips, for something like an eagle is over Yahweh's house, because they have broken his covenant.

answers.text: Something like an eagle
A cloud of smoke
A swarm of locusts
A host of horsemen

questions.text: What do they cry to Yahweh, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says they cry to him, my God, we Israel acknowledge you.

answers.text: Save us, for the enemy is at the gate
Remember the covenant you made with us
My God, we Israel acknowledge you
Give us a king to judge us as the nations have

questions.text: What does Yahweh say about the kings and princes they have set up?
questions.explanation: The verse says they have set up kings but not by him, and made princes without his approval, and made idols of their silver and gold.

answers.text: They were anointed by his own prophets
They were set up without him, and he did not approve
They were taken away before he could act
They were chosen from the house of Judah

questions.text: What does this chapter say will happen to the calf of Samaria?
questions.explanation: The verses say Samaria is to throw out his calf idol, that the workman made it and it is no God, and that the calf of Samaria will be broken in pieces.

answers.text: It will be carried into the wilderness
It will be melted down for the king
It will be set up in Yahweh's house
It will be broken in pieces

questions.text: What does this chapter say they sow and what will they reap?
questions.explanation: The verse says they sow the wind and will reap the whirlwind, and that the stalk will yield no head.

answers.text: They sow the wind and will reap the whirlwind
They sow in tears and will reap in joy
They sow wheat and will reap thorns
They sow thorns and will reap stubble

questions.text: What are they compared with when they have gone up to Assyria?
questions.explanation: The verse says they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey wandering alone, and that Ephraim has hired lovers for himself.

answers.text: A lost sheep without a shepherd
A bird caught in a snare
A wild donkey wandering alone
A heifer led to the threshing floor

questions.text: What has Ephraim multiplied, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, and that they became for him altars for sinning.

answers.text: Fortified cities
Altars for sinning
Chariots and horses
Prophets and priests

questions.text: How were the many things of Yahweh's law regarded, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says he wrote for him the many things of his law, but they were regarded as a strange thing.

answers.text: As a heavy burden
As a sealed book
As a word of the prophets
As a strange thing

questions.text: Where does this chapter say they will return, after their sacrifices are not accepted?
questions.explanation: The verse says Yahweh does not accept their sacrifices, that he will remember their iniquity and punish their sins, and that they will return to Egypt.

answers.text: To Egypt
To Assyria
To Gilgal
To the wilderness

questions.text: What has Israel forgotten and built, in the last verse of the chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces, while Judah has multiplied fortified cities, and a fire will be sent on his cities.

answers.text: He has forgotten his king and built altars
He has forgotten his law and built high places
He has forgotten his Maker and built palaces
He has forgotten his brothers and built walls
